item.text: {"question_id":"5B.7","answer":"During 2023, the government had formal and programme-level mechanisms for monitoring, evaluation, budget control, audit, and publication. The CPVS, chaired by Tshisekedi, tracked presidential commitments and acknowledged implementation difficulties, while the education ministry held an annual performance review focused on reform implementation and prior recommendations (BATCH-0020-E011; BATCH-0020-E012; BATCH-0023-E006). The government also participated in validation of an education-system diagnostic, and World Bank analytical work informed education-strategy review and project design (BATCH-0009-E006; BATCH-0026-E009). The PDL-145T government reported that citizens would be able to monitor projects by telephone, but the supplied evidence does not show actual use or independent verification (BATCH-0023-E003). The budget-governance decree established requirements for independent and objective internal audit, risk committees, follow-up of audit recommendations, and publication of detailed budget and execution information; however, it is evidence of formal safeguards rather than proof of timely publication, operational independence, or compliance (BATCH-0029-E005). Tshisekedi also directed the government, central bank, and financial inspectorate to implement exchange-rate and fiscal-control measures, but the supplied evidence does not establish their effectiveness or a correction based on measured results (BATCH-0024-E005). He publicly acknowledged declining purchasing power and attributed limited felt benefits to global and security conditions, but this presidential account lacks independent measurement and does not itself demonstrate corrective action (BATCH-0015-E004). Countervailing evidence shows that an external evaluation found only half of planned activities fully implemented and weak coordination among monitoring teams; its recommendations are not shown as adopted by the government (BATCH-0002-E001; BATCH-0002-E004; BATCH-0002-E005). Later parliamentary review of the 2023 accounts, citing Court of Accounts observations, identified noncompliance, excessive overruns, uncertified debts, and works reported without observed concrete action, but the supplied material does not show that Tshisekedi personally directed those failures or that identified implementers were corrected (BATCH-0024-E003; BATCH-0024-E004). Overall, the evidence supports the existence of formal monitoring and evidence-oriented processes, plus some acknowledgment of problems, but does not establish reliable public information in practice, consistently independent evaluation, or consequence-linked correction across the economic system.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E011","BATCH-0020-E012","BATCH-0023-E006","BATCH-0009-E006","BATCH-0026-E009","BATCH-0023-E003","BATCH-0029-E005","BATCH-0024-E005","BATCH-0015-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E001","BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E005","BATCH-0024-E003","BATCH-0024-E004"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most favorable evidence concerns official mechanisms, programme plans, diagnostics, or policy design rather than independently verified operation or outcomes.","The supplied evidence does not establish that budget information was published on time, that audits were independent in practice, or that evaluation findings led to completed corrective action.","Several adverse findings concern institutions or government systems rather than personally attributable presidential decisions.","The period is primarily 2023, with the WFP evaluation conducted in 2023–2024 and the budget-account review reported in 2024 about 2023 execution.","The evidence does not directly establish reliance on slogans, denial, patronage, or scapegoating; absence of demonstrated correction should not be overstated as proof of those practices."],"corrections_made":["Recast monitoring structures, official reviews, announced mechanisms, and legal safeguards as evidence of intended or formal capacity rather than proof of reliable information, independent evaluation, or completed correction.","Retained the formal budget-governance, education, CPVS, PDL-145T, and macroeconomic evidence while preserving each source's attribution and implementation limits.","Removed the electoral-register audit evidence as irrelevant to this economic evidence-and-correction question.","Qualified the parliamentary and programme failures so they are not treated as personally directed by Tshisekedi without direct attribution.","Separated acknowledgment of problems and announced measures from verified, consequence-linked corrective action."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Obtain evidence of actual 2023 publication and accessibility of budget and execution information under the decree.","Verify whether internal or external audits and programme evaluations were completed, independent, publicly available, and followed by documented corrective decisions.","Establish whether the PDL-145T monitoring tool was operational and whether project data were complete and independently checked.","Trace the implementation and measured effects of the July 2023 exchange-rate and fiscal measures.","Identify any direct presidential or ministerial responses to the WFP and Court of Accounts findings."]}
